text:
alex: Heads up — eu3 dedicated pool reporting 96% GPU allocation and growing, eviction spikes on low-priority orgs since 12:07 UTC. queues/backpressure visible in shard metrics.
maya: seeing the same in the dashboards, tail latency creeping up for short requests. which pools are saturated?
alex: nodegroup-eu3-pt1 and -pt2. roughly 220 active jobs queued, avg wait ~1.6s, but a lot of short chat requests are timing out in the client.
juan: capacity-bot just posted an auto-fallback: fallback-policy=hosted-absorb, threshold=90%, reason=dedicated-overcommit. Did it already flip routing weights?
capacity-bot: auto-fallback executed at 1937654300. Routing weights updated: dedicated eu3 0.70 -> 0.45, hosted eu 0.30 -> 0.55 for low-priority tag. Canary window 5m.
rachel: okay good. do we have a list of orgs tagged low-priority? want to make sure no SLA customers get shifted.
alex: confirmed list: [nice-to-have, sandbox, internal-devs], not production tiers. double-checked with oncall-lisa.
oncall-lisa: confirmed. no premium SLA orgs in the low-priority bucket for eu3. monitoring alerts sent to owners.
maya: cost question — if hosted picks up ~25% of eu3 steady traffic for the next 6 hours, ballpark increment = +$2.3k. finance pinged?
juan: pinged finance in #finance, they'll get the postmortem cost note. For now, focus on stability.
alex: plan: 1) keep hosted weight increased for low-priority for the next 15m canary. 2) trigger scale-up for dedicated eu3 spot pool (+4 p4d) if capacity providers available. 3) throttle non-interactive batch jobs by setting max_concurrency=2 for low-priority labels. 4) re-evaluate in 30m.
maya: commands to run for the weight change if we need manual rollback:

```
curl -X POST https://controlplane.internal/api/v1/routing/set_weights \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $CP_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"region":"eu3","weights":{"dedicated":0.45,"hosted":0.55},"selector":"priority:low"}'
```

juan: for scale-up I started an infra ticket to request 4x p4d on eu3. If cloud has limits we'll need to keep fallback running.
rachel: I'll flip the batch throttles via the job controller:

```
kubectl -n workloads patch jobqueue low-priority -p '{"spec":{"maxConcurrency":2}}'
```

alex: quick sanity: run `kubectl get nodes -l pool=eu3-pt -o wide` and `infractl capacity describe eu3` if you need node details.
oncall-lisa: doing a rolling health check on nodegroup-eu3-pt1 now. reporting back in ~3m.
capacity-bot: healthcheck eu3-pt1: 2 nodes reporting GPU mem pressure, 1 node under eviction threshold, mean GPU util 94%.
maya: rx. if evictions persist we should mark the offending nodes cordoned and drain non-critical pods to reduce churn.
juan: note: some customers in low-priority are opt-in for hosted fallback — their requests will see higher token-cost but preserve availability. Keep analytics tag on to measure regen rates.
rachel: can we set a temporary rate-limit on retries? failing fast reduces load.
alex: yes: add retry_backoff_ms=300 and max_retries=1 for low-priority clients via the edge config. I'll push the change.
oncall-lisa: health check done: pt1 still marginal, pt2 warming down slightly after fallback. overall latencies stabilizing.
maya: canary window passed (15m). metrics show queue length down 70% and error rate down 85% for low-priority. shall we gradually move weights back or keep hosted elevated until scale-up completes?
alex: keep hosted elevated until we confirm new nodes active. target: bring dedicated back to 80% weight after scale completes and 10m stable.
juan: reminder: update incident tracker and tag with cost_estimate and fallback_reason. I'll draft a short note for #status when we close.
capacity-bot: snapshot saved: snapshot_id=eu3-1937654405, metrics window=15m, queues reduced.
rachel: on the follow-up: we should add an autoscale policy tweak — increase reserved buffer for low-priority spike windows, and add a preemptive warmup when utilization hits 85% for 5m.
alex: agree. filing RFC for policy change, will include cost vs availability tradeoffs. For now, monitoring/close after new nodes online.
maya: ack. nice run — minimal user impact. will follow up with cost memo.
juan: closing loop: if dedicated can't scale due to provider limits, we should consider temporary cross-region spill to eu1 hosted pools + adjust regional latency hints.
oncall-lisa: noted, I'll keep pager on for next 2h. if we see util >95% again, escalate to emergency provisioning.
alex: thanks all. update incident thread when weights return to baseline. :thumbsup:
